chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Jabalah narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who makes fasting obligatory upon himself in a vow, but is unable, he said: "He gives to one who fasts on his behalf two mudds for each day."

key_terms.صِيَامًا: fasting made binding in the vow
key_terms.فَلَا يَقْوَى: he is unable or lacks the strength to perform it
key_terms.مُدَّيْنِ: two mudds, a measured quantity of food
key_terms.نَذْرٍ: a vow by which a person obligates an act upon himself

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he vowed to fast but is unable to fulfill the vow?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person who vowed to fast but is unable to carry it out. The Imam عليه السلام states that he should give two mudds for each day to someone who will fast on his behalf, showing a compensatory arrangement in the case of incapacity.
